_comment: Barnaby Coil. Dry, precise, short sentences; states an opinion once. Calls the player 'topper'. Never says Wren's name until he has to.

lines.text: The Lease is west, past the farm plots. Bed, bench, a tin of seeds. Go on. I'll be here, losing to a pump.
Glass up at the well, topper. [{key:cut_view}] The break's under the lane somewhere. Seal gum for a crack, pipe for a hole.
The valve's in the Sink, under the hall. Through the glass, topper. I'll be there before you are. I've been there for eleven years.
You fell asleep on the moss again. Next time I'm leaving you for the lice.
There's water going where water shouldn't. I can hear it. So can the rock, and the rock remembers.
You can taste it in the lane. Somebody's breathing out of turn, and it isn't the Deep.
Exhale day. Keep your vents high and your expectations low.
Burner's warm. You'll have friends at the Exchange and fewer at the lake. That's not a criticism. It's a weather report.
That turbine. Quiet as a held breath. I approve, and I'd like that written down somewhere.
A crank. Good. Nothing teaches you what a watt is like turning one by hand.
Smelled hot copper last night. Wire's like a mule. Ask it to carry too much and it sits down. Then it catches fire.
The fissure's still open. Gas doesn't get bored and go home, topper. Pack it.
Mags asked me who's been fixing her line at night. Said I had no idea. Said it very well, I thought.
Tea first. Then problems. Then more tea, as a treat.
Well's holding. I went and looked at it twice this morning. Don't make it a thing.
Glowroots peak at Bloom. Best light there is to read a gauge by. Worst light to read a person.
Lantern House is loud tonight. I'll be the quiet table. There's always one.
I'm walking. It's a thing people do. At night. With wrenches.
You've got a face like you're about to say 'should be easy'. Don't.
The moss in the crack? Grew there on its own. I'd scrape it off but it's the only thing that's ever chosen me.
Odile thinks in numbers. It's not a flaw. It's just loud.
Hesper would rather the town choked than a lichen sneezed. She's wrong. She's also not entirely wrong.
Topper.
Mind the pipe-heads.
Hm.
Cold morning. Hands don't like it.
Gauges don't lie. People do. Gauges learn it from people.
Come on, you wretched— no. Nothing.
Smell that? No? Lucky.
Three. Two. Three.

intro.say: —come on, you wretched, ungrateful— oh. Hello.
You came down the shaft. Hard way. Cable's been fraying for a year, and nobody up top reads letters.
Barnaby. I keep the water running, when it runs. Today it doesn't.

choice.text: Is there a way back up?

intro.say: Somewhere between here and the cistern the line's drinking itself. Find where, mend it. Easy to say. I've been saying it all morning.
There's a way up the way there's a way to the moon. Not this week.
The Lease. West end, past the farm plots. Tolley went down-line. Doesn't need it.
Bed, bench, and a tin of seeds he wouldn't shut up about. Go on, topper.

glass.say: Settled in? Good. Bad news: the beets will want water, and the well wants a priest.
I've traced it this far. Dry from here to the cistern. Something below's drinking it.
Here. Plumb-glass. Old Trunk crew kit. Surveyors used them before there was nothing left to survey.
Hold it up at the well [{key:cut_view}] and look at the ground the way the pipe sees it.
Seal gum for a crack. Pipe for a hole. If it's both, come and tell me, and I'll pretend to be surprised.
I know what's down there. That's the trouble with looking. You keep seeing it after.

well_fixed.say: Water in the basin. Real water. I put my hand in it to check. Don't tell anyone.
That line's older than me, which says something about the line.
Here's the thing. The cistern feeds everyone, and nothing feeds the cistern. The Station pump used to.
Give it a week and it's mud. We'll want a pump of our own down in the Sink. And a pump wants power.
You did good work. I'm only going to say that the once, so I'd write it down.

power.say: Power. Three ways to get it. Every one costs something.
Odile will sell you a burner. Burns beets or resin. Strong and steady, and it breathes out sour air. The lake won't thank you.
Hesper will tell you the spring at the east wall falls far enough to turn a turbine. Clean. Quiet. Weak, unless you're clever about where you put it.
Or a crank. Builds character. Mine's mostly built.
I'd pick the one I could fix at three in the morning with cold hands. But I'm not you, and you'll be up at three in the morning either way.
Whatever you pick: pump low in the Sink, pipe up to the cistern outlet. Water's lazy. It wants help going up.

reach.say: You've been looking at the Reach gate like it owes you money.
Down there's where the parts are. Brass, glowglass, the odd thing nobody should've left behind.
Take this. Hammer's for rock, not for Knappers.
If you meet a Knapper, be slow and be kind. They've got better hearing than manners, and better manners than us.
Be home before Hush. If you're not, I'll come looking, and I'll be insufferable about it.

station_look.say: I need you to do something. Not a favour. A look.
The Station pump. In the hall. Bring the glass. Just look at it.
Eleven years it's been dead. I know what it needs. I'd like somebody else to tell me I'm wrong.
Because if I go in there with the glass, I'll see the valve. Go on. Please.

station_seen.say: Governor coil's gone. Seals are dust. The rest is just old, and old isn't broken. I knew that. I wanted to hear it in someone else's voice.
There was a spare coil. In the Trunk chamber, down past the Sump. The passage collapsed in the flood. Or I collapsed it. The days run together.
So that's that. Unless the rock changes its mind.

rounds.say: ...With a wrench. And seal gum. Next to Mags' line. Which has a crack in it. Coincidentally.
Don't make a face. If I fix it in daylight, it becomes my job. At night it's a hobby.
Wren used to hold the lamp. Talked the whole time. Couldn't hear the pipe for her.
It's not a secret. It's a hobby. Goodnight, topper.

tremor.say: You felt it. Everyone felt it. Grist's been saying the rock was singing wrong for a season.
Lines are cracked all down the lane. And the sour pocket under the Lease has found a way up.
Sour gas is heavy. It pools in the low places. Cellars. Plots. Hesper's beds.
Pack the fissure with blackstone, or scrub the air, or move your crops. Pick one. Today.
...And the Sump flooded. Which means the old Trunk passage is open again. Which means the coil is in reach.
Funny. I spent eleven years hoping that wouldn't happen.

wren.say: ...The locker. Of course. I never opened it. Couldn't.
Wren Askew. Trunk crew. My partner. She was down-line when the Sump flood came up the Trunk.
The valve had to close or Wick drowned. It only closes from this side. I closed it.
She knocked for an hour. Three, two, three. Crew code for 'still here'.
That's what they tell me. It's a fine sentence. I've worn it smooth.
Down there? Eleven years? No. ...The tag's warm, though. Isn't it.
...Thank you. People always want to say something.
Keep it. I'd only put it in a drawer and look at the drawer.

wren_note.say: You've got a look. Like you've read something you'd rather I read first.
'Stop that face.' She'd say that. She'd say it every time.
A dry stair. Pumps running below. And she went to see. Of course she went to see.
Eleven years I've been sitting at the quiet table with the wrong grief. Not the dead kind. The left-behind kind.
Thank you, topper. I mean it. I'm going to go and be somewhere else for a bit.

coil.say: Is that— that's a governor coil. A real one. Not a rumour.
Fit it. Four seal gum on the housing. Feed the pump fifty-five power, and the Station will run.
...And then the hall will have pressure, and the gauge will want to read, and somebody will have to look at that valve.
One thing at a time. The pump first. The valve can wait. It's very good at it.

valve.say: Listen to it. Eleven years of nothing, and it purrs like it was waiting for us.
Cistern'll be full by morning. Wick won't be thirsty again in my lifetime. Which is a smaller promise than it sounds.
And the gauge by the valve moved. LOWER STATIONS. There's pressure on the far side.
There shouldn't be. Not after eleven years. Not unless something down there is running.

choice.text: Leave it shut. Wick comes first.

valve.say: ...Yes. I suppose we should. If it floods, I'll close it again. I've had practice.
That's what I said, eleven years ago. Sensible. I've hated it every day since. ...We'll listen, then. Listening's allowed.
It was always mine. That was the trouble. ...Come with me. I'll do it, but not alone.
The valve's in the Sink, under the hall. Meet me there. Through the glass.

finale_open.say: ...I always hated 'on three'. Is it on three, or after three? Wren and I argued about it for a year.
The wheel gives. Copper wire parts with a sound like a held breath let go. Far below, the dark sighs.
Nothing. Of course. Eleven years. What did I think—
Up the pipe, faint and perfectly clear: three knocks. Two. Three.
Topper. There is someone down there.

finale_shut.say: You press your ear to the cold iron. Barnaby does the same, on the other side of the wheel, not looking at you.
Nothing. Of course. What did I think I'd—
Through the iron, against your cheek: three knocks. Two. Three.
Crew code. 'Still here.' Knocked on the far side of a valve I sealed, by someone who knows the code.
Well. I suppose we're going to need a bigger plan than 'leave it shut'.

after.say: I keep listening for it. The knock. Every pipe in Wick sounds like a question now.
The Trunk goes down a long way. Further than the maps. Further than the Lower Stations, if Wren's right, and she was always right about the inconvenient things.
We'd need light. Air. A way back up. Sleep on it, topper.
...I'm going to sleep in the pump hall tonight. Somebody should be near the gauge.
